$comment: Traceability from public claims on the Blueprint page to the control framework that
backs them, at framework/controls.yaml in the thebehumancompany repository.
The point is not documentation. Sales copy about governance drifts from the thing it
describes one confident sentence at a time, and nothing catches it, because prose has
no compiler. Every claim below names the control ids it rests on; a test asserts each
id resolves in the real YAML and that at least eight domains are represented, so a
claim that outgrew its evidence — or an id that was renamed underneath it — fails
POSITIONING, WHICH IS BINDING: controls.yaml's own meta.positioning says the framework
is readiness and assurance, NOT a compliance guarantee, and that the Maturity Score is
NOT a certification. Copy may describe what is assessed. It may not promise an outcome
the framework itself declines to promise.
SOVEREIGNTY ASSERTS NO DEFINITION, deliberately. controls.yaml records a signed-off
divergence: it rescoped sovereignty from hosting geography to data handling, and its
declared source of truth has not been updated to match. While those two disagree, any
definition published here would contradict one of them. So the claims below describe
practices that are assessed and evidenced, and never say what sovereignty is.

claims.claim: We uncover governance gaps and trace how data actually moves through AI systems.
Shadow AI exposure is assessed rather than assumed: which tools are in use, what data reaches them, and who is accountable.
We look at whether no-train and no-retention terms are contractually in place with the providers already in use.
We look at whether personal and confidential data is redacted at the model boundary by a control, rather than by instructing people.
We look at whether model and tool calls are recorded in a retained, reviewable audit trail.
We look at whether the business controls the encryption keys for sensitive AI data.
We look at whether there is an exit and portability plan, including deletion of the provider's copy.
Processing location and legal jurisdiction are treated as one recorded, rationalized factor in a data-handling decision — not as the whole question.
No client-facing output is delivered without a human who has reviewed it and stands behind it.
AI can inform a decision. It never owns the judgment.
If your information will pass through non-Canadian AI infrastructure, you will know before it happens.
Every AI system we build or recommend has a named person responsible for its direction and outcomes.
The Risk & Governance Review covers shadow AI exposure, data flows, governance gaps, cybersecurity concerns, and sovereignty considerations — with what to address first.
Executive Findings covers leadership readiness and employee AI usage.
Each ranked AI opportunity carries a recommended human owner.
Your information is used solely to complete your Blueprint. It is not used to train our systems or anyone else's.
